Laura / Kate — joined the bridge. Initial triage summary (07:02 PT):

What we see
- Error pattern: OOMs observed in inferencer containers followed by node restarts. Error traces show repeated KV cache expansion for long-prefix sequences (customer workload has extreme long-context prefixes).
- Full nodes affected: us-west-2-gpupool-12 and -13. These nodes hit memory pressure at ~06:04 and then restarted under kube OOMKill.
- Latency bump was due to repeated cold starts + reloading model weights.

Immediate mitigations performed (07:02–07:25):
1) Enabled emergency fallback routing for Orbit Apps to the cpu-fallback-pool to keep prediction traffic flowing (rate-limited to avoid cascading latency).
2) Rolled back the last quantized variant rollout that increased KV footprint for long prefixes; pinned to the previous release.
3) Soft purge of long-prefix entries from KV cache for Orbit's tenant keys to free memory (script run, retained hot prefixes).
4) Drained and repaired us-west-2-gpupool-13; restarted containers and confirmed model hot-loading.

Impact: fallback routing kept success rate > 96% but with higher p95 latency (~900ms). We anticipate restoring GPU path in the next 30–60 minutes as nodes stabilize.

Next steps (owner):
- hannah_schmitt: continue health checks, full log dump to S3, host-level metrics dashboard link below.
- marcus_lin: coordinate customer-side canary traffic and gather any recent model/rollout notes from Orbit.
- laura_bennett: executive-facing update and credits/compensation note for Kate and execs.

Attachments: syslog excerpt from us-west-2-gpupool-13 (syslog_excerpt_20261020.txt)

Hi Kate / Ethan — thank you again for your patience this morning. Quick executive summary and next steps:

Summary of impact
- Window: 06:03–07:18 PT
- User-facing effect: transient errors and increased latency affecting payment-scoring calls; Orbit saw ~18% error rate at peak, mitigated to <4% after fallback routing.
- Root cause (preliminary): a memory-pressure cascade in us-west-2 GPU pool triggered by unbounded KV cache growth when handling very long prefix sequences after a quantized variant rollout. This led to OOMKills, container restarts, and repeat cold starts.

What we did (in-moment)
- Immediate fallback to CPU pool to stabilize traffic and preserve correctness.
- Rolled back the quantized variant that expanded per-request KV usage.
- Purged long-prefix KV entries for Orbit's tenant to reclaim memory without affecting typical hot prefixes.
- Repaired and validated the GPU nodes; services progressively returned to normal.

Short-term action items (next 72 hours)
- Full postmortem and technical write-up (owner: hannah_schmitt). ETA: 2026-10-22 17:00 PT.
- Remediation: add hard limits on per-tenant KV cache allocations and a guardrail on quantized rollout criteria (owner: infra runtime team).
- Customer follow-up: TAM-led canary resume plan and coordinated rollout to re-enable GPU path under measurement (owner: marcus_lin).
- Compensation: Laura to share a good-faith credits proposal for the impacted hour window and mitigation effort (attachment: credits_agreement_draft.docx).

We have attached the immediate recovery playbook used this morning for your records (recovery_playbook_v1.pdf) and a syslog excerpt highlighting the OOM events (syslog_excerpt_20261020.txt).

Proposed postmortem cadence
- Technical deep-dive (Hannah + Infra): 2026-10-21 09:00 PT (invite to Orbit technical leads).
- Executive review & commercial resolution (Laura + Kate + Marcus): 2026-10-22 11:00 PT.

Please let me know if either of those times conflict and I will adjust. Marcus will follow up on the canary plan once we confirm the remediation windows.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we prioritise reliability and will share concrete remediation and compensation terms in the postmortem.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Customer Success Manager
